g1-implement.title: The generator: implement
g1-implement.imperative: Fill the implementer handoff from this gate plan and dispatch a Sonnet implementer through scripts/run_crew.py. Deliverable: ONE file, scripts/generate_spine.py -- pure compile_spec/compile_condition (dict in, dict out; no Path, no open, no subprocess) with the CLI, the generation-time probes and main() below them, matching the function-granularity pure/impure split validate_spine.py and checklist_engine.py already use. Five closed check kinds: qualitative (requires a non-empty `because`), pytest (selector + min_collect + targets -> the corpus self-checking idiom, selector shlex.quote'd, anchored `cd <repo-root> &&`), script (path + args -> shlex.join, anchored, probed by ast.parse of the target's add_argument literals, NEVER importing it), population (root + glob + expected band, probed by EXECUTING the compiled command itself so the thing probed is the thing shipped), artifact (evidence_type + match). No raw-command field exists anywhere in the format. Every gate gets the handback directives contract; a [gate.claim] magnitude=large injects an artifact/review-result check matching verdict APPROVE plus a claims_rollup on the terminal gate. validate() is called as the literal last statement before success and any Fault or any .undecidable entry refuses with nothing written. Read .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/DESIGN_NOTE.md first; it is frozen.

why_trail.why: The plan's first act found a defect in the plan's own machinery, twice. The MCP door binds exactly one spine at import time (mcp_spine_server.py:106) and offers no per-call addressing, so a Commander cannot drive its own execute.json through the door at all -- the very step the shipped Commander spine tells it to. Flagged as tc1 on my spine and floated; execute.json is driven through checklist_engine.py directly, journaled, as the closest compliant thing. Second: config_ref pointing at a file that EXISTS but is not JSON crashes load_config with an unhandled JSONDecodeError before any rail text prints, and validate_spine.py does not catch that shape -- a fault class the lint misses and my generator should refuse. Both are recorded rather than smoothed over, and the second is now a design input for g0.

Freezing the vocabulary surfaced two things the plan had not settled. First, decision:qualitative-must-be-stated had no mechanism -- the lint's message offers the stated form as an out but nothing makes an author take it. Appending the required 'because' text into the emitted statement makes it mechanical: a gate with no checkable postcondition cannot be emitted without saying in the spine itself that it is qualitative and why. Second, I hit spec-config-ref-not-json live while wiring this very plan: load_config json.loads ANY config_ref that exists, so pointing it at a markdown file crashed the engine with an unhandled JSONDecodeError before any rail text could print, and validate_spine.py has no fault for that shape. That is a real gap in the oracle, and it becomes a spec-shape fault the generator refuses -- without moving the oracle, which is not mine to move.

The implementer built scripts/generate_spine.py (597 lines) and tests/test_generate_spine.py (76 tests), suite 2765 passed / 3 skipped / 1121 subtests, sweep still 23. The result is honest in the two places that matter most: the wiring grep says plainly that NOTHING outside its own test file calls the generator yet, and the ACCEPTED_FALSE_ALARM for the population probe was corrected mid-cycle because the crew had assumed Path.glob excludes dotfiles, measured it, and found the opposite -- it nearly reproduced this epic's own defect shape inside its guard fixture and said so. Seven decisions were made where DESIGN_NOTE.md was silent; all seven look right to me and none contradicts the note. Not yet reviewed: a cold reviewer runs next, and I will not accept the control pairing until someone other than its author has re-run it.

Cold reviewer independent of the implementer returned APPROVE with no blockers, and it earned the verdict by RUNNING things rather than reading: it built its own control-pairing fixture rather than re-running the implementer's, proved purity with an independent ast.walk instead of eyeballing, gave the script probe a target whose import-time code both raises AND writes a sentinel file and confirmed neither happened, re-ran the mutation floor with its own harness, and measured both ACCEPTED_FALSE_ALARM premises live instead of trusting the docstring. It found one thing the implementer had not claimed: _RESOLVER_OWNED_TOKEN_RE is imported and never used, so the design note's justification for emitting <repo-root> is asserted in prose and wired to nothing. Carried into g2 as a required cleanup -- turned into a real assertion rather than deleted, so the claim gets pinned by a test.

Verified the crew's claimed side-effects against the world rather than accepting the claim. I re-ran the control pairing with MY OWN spec (a script check carrying <not-a-resolver-token>): the pure path translates it without complaint and spec_shape_faults returns [], the guarded CLI refuses it with the oracle's own falsifiable-unresolved-placeholder text at exit 4, and test ! -f confirmed nothing was written; the same spec corrected is written, anchored cd <repo-root> &&, carrying the handback contract. I also compiled my own two-gate large-claim spec and confirmed c-escalation is injected with check artifact/review-result match verdict APPROVE, that the rollup lands on the LAST gate keyed by source, and that it is absent from the earlier gate. The engine re-ran both command postconditions on this advance: the full suite in the declared test mode and the sweep guard asserting the shipped corpus still reports exactly 23 fault lines. The generator exists, refuses what the oracle would refuse, and carries both non-optional properties -- but it is wired to nothing outside its own tests, which the crew said plainly and which g2 is what closes.

Both role specs exist, both generate, both generated spines are OK under the oracle with zero undecidable, and the shipped <exact test command> placeholder is gone -- replaced by a selector and a number. The crew reported the suite as 1 failed and judged the failure pre-existing by stashing its own changes; I checked that inference rather than accepting it, and it was subtly wrong in the direction that matters. The failure is map/INDEX.md staleness at 57 modules vs 56 committed, and the extra module is scripts/generate_spine.py -- added by g1, i.e. caused by THIS run, not by the branch base. Stashing g2's changes could never have revealed that, because g1 was already committed underneath. I regenerated with python -m scripts.code_map build and the suite is now fully green at 2767 passed / 3 skipped / 1121 subtests. The lesson is the authoring-side twin of verify-side-effects: adding a module silently invalidates every artifact that asserts something about the module set, and the author is the one who does not look. The settling question came back answered with a real residual: the script kind's probe never inspects POSITIONAL arguments, only --flag tokens, so r6-fowler's path argument is still only as good as the author's own reading of the target script.

The cold reviewer returned BLOCK and earned it by driving the mechanism rather than inspecting its shape. It copied the generated reviewer survey to scratch, resolved the tokens, drove every item through record, and consolidated -- and the survey consolidated APPROVE with the injected c-escalation postcondition still unsatisfied and no review-result ever attached. Reading the engine explains it: record() filters to command-kind postconditions on a survey item (#422/#328) and consolidate() reads only each item's result field, while advance() on a gated gate checks every postcondition with no kind filter. So Property 2 -- one of the two non-optional properties of this whole mission -- is enforced on gated gates and SILENTLY INERT on survey gates, which is where this spec's own author put the claim. My own DESIGN_NOTE named a narrower residual (a determined agent could attach a spoofed APPROVE); the real gap is worse -- nothing needs to be attached at all. Neither the implementer's JSON-shape evidence nor its Finding 6 caught it, because both looked at the artifact instead of running it.

A spine generated by scripts/generate_spine.py was dispatched with run_crew.py --spine and no handoff and no result path, and reached a terminal state: both items complete, lease released, run_crew judging it on spine_terminal. That is protected intent #4, proven with a real dispatch rather than a simulation. Two things happened on the way that are worth more than the proof itself. First, the crew BLOCKED a gate instead of forcing it, and it was right: I had authored m1.c2 as a script check omitting --out, which argparse marks required unconditionally, so the check exited 2 before a spec was ever opened and could never pass. The generator did not catch it, because the script probe verifies that every flag an author NAMED exists and cannot see a required flag the author FAILED to name -- defect 3's twin, found in the mission's own machinery, authored by me. Second, the durable handback path worked exactly as E1 predicted: a blocked gate, a recorded parent, and a parent that polls. No message was needed. I resumed the gate, repaired the check through amend/retext-check under my own authority, and relaunched a fresh crew into the same job file, which drove it to terminal. Also found: recover_crews.py misclassifies the completed spine-only dispatch as NEEDS-ABANDON because its classifier keys on a result artifact a spine-only crew deliberately never writes -- flagged as tc2.

APPROVE with no surviving findings, and the reviewer earned it by answering the question I could not review myself. On the adjudication it found four converging reasons the repair was legitimate: the check was provably wrong on its own terms and would fail identically for a perfect implementation, and retext-check is the narrowly-scoped sanctioned tool for exactly that. On what the proof establishes it was sharper than my own framing: spine_terminal is a purely structural predicate, so a spine authored with only qualitative postconditions could reach it on attestation alone -- that WOULD be a check that cannot fail. This dispatch's proof is real because this spine gated its substantive postcondition behind a command check the engine itself runs by subprocess, with produced_by engine on the resulting evidence. So protected intent #4 is proven for this dispatch, not as a property of the completion contract. That qualification goes in the return report verbatim rather than being rounded up.

The dispatch proof holds and its limits are stated rather than rounded up. The engine re-ran all three postconditions on this advance: the full suite, the reviewer's APPROVE, and the terminal-state check read from the spine the dispatch actually drove. What this gate really bought was not the proof but the two defects it exposed on the way -- my own missing-required-flag check, which the generator emitted and the oracle accepted, and recover_crews misclassifying a completed spine-only dispatch. Both are in the run packet as classified discrepancies rather than quietly fixed.
